title: Star Voyager
description: Star Voyager is an original vector-flight game about a lone survey ship mapping a quiet corner of space. The ship drifts among slow, bright rocks, and its beam can break them apart for points. The field is calm, the stars are still, and the whole game feels like a careful walk through a dark gallery.
body:
Star Voyager is an original vector-flight game about a lone survey ship mapping a quiet corner of space. The ship drifts among slow, bright rocks, and its beam can break them apart for points. The field is calm, the stars are still, and the whole game feels like a careful walk through a dark gallery.

The rules are simple: turn left or right, thrust to glide two steps in the direction you face, and shoot to break rocks up to three steps ahead. You have three lives, and touching a rock costs one. The demo plays a short flight with two clean hits and a few honest misses.

Voyager pilots fly in straight lines and shoot from range. Line up on a rock row, fire until it breaks, and thrust clear before the next rock drifts near. The survey rewards a steady hand far more than a fast one.
controls: Type thrust/left/right/shoot to fly and fire, quit to stop.

title: Paddle Clash
description: Paddle Clash is an original paddle game about two rivals meeting under festival lights for a single rally. You guard the left wall with a short paddle while the ball bounces around the court, and every return you make scores a point. The rally is fast, the court is small, and the crowd counts every return out loud.
body:
Paddle Clash is an original paddle game about two rivals meeting under festival lights for a single rally. You guard the left wall with a short paddle while the ball bounces around the court, and every return you make scores a point. The rally is fast, the court is small, and the crowd counts every return out loud.

The rules are direct: move the paddle up, down, or hold it still each tick, and meet the ball when it reaches your wall. A return scores for you; a ball that slips past scores for the other side and resets the rally. The demo plays one scripted rally that ends with the player one point ahead.

Clash players hold the middle and move late. The paddle starts in the center of its travel, and the winning move is a small step made at the last moment, not a long chase across the court. Players who waited won rallies; players who flailed lost them.

title: Brick Buster Brigade
description: Brick Buster Brigade is an original paddle game about a neighborhood crew that breaks bricks for fun. You guard the left wall with a paddle, and the rally's rhythm stands in for the satisfying crack of brick after brick. The brigade's motto is simple: keep the ball alive, and the wall comes down one brick at a time.

Brick Buster Brigade is an original paddle game about a neighborhood crew that breaks bricks for fun. You guard the left wall with a paddle, and the rally's rhythm stands in for the satisfying crack of brick after brick. The brigade's motto is simple: keep the ball alive, and the wall comes down one brick at a time.

The rules are the paddle rules: move up, down, or hold still each tick, and meet the ball at your wall. A return keeps the rally going and scores a point; a miss ends the rally and hands the point to the other side. The demo plays a rally that ends in a miss, because the brigade's real lesson is starting over wiser after a loss.

Brigade players watch the ball, not the paddle. Tracking the ball's path lets you position the paddle before the ball arrives, while watching only the paddle leaves you a step behind every time. Look ahead, move little, and the bricks fall.

title: Moon Invaders
description: Moon Invaders is an original fixed shooter about defending a moon base from descending sky fragments. Five columns of fragments in two rows drift down toward the base, and your ground cannon slides along the ridge to blast them. The sky clears column by column, and the base holds as long as the cannon keeps firing.
body:
Moon Invaders is an original fixed shooter about defending a moon base from descending sky fragments. Five columns of fragments in two rows drift down toward the base, and your ground cannon slides along the ridge to blast them. The sky clears column by column, and the base holds as long as the cannon keeps firing.

The rules are clean: move left or right, fire upward, and clear every fragment before it reaches the ground line. A shot destroys the lowest fragment in your column, so finishing one column before starting the next is the fastest path to a clear sky. The demo plays a perfect defense that clears all ten fragments.

Column discipline is everything. A half-cleared column is a distraction, while a fully cleared column never threatens you again. Work from the edges inward, move between shots, and the moon base will still be standing when the sky empties.
controls: Type left/right/shoot to move and fire, quit to stop.

description: Lunar Descent is an original vector-flight game about guiding a small lander down a cliff face to a flat landing pad. Gravity pulls constantly, thrust comes in short bursts, and the pad is small, so the descent must be planned from the top. The game is quiet and tense, with no enemies, only the ground and the pilot's own judgment.

Lunar Descent is an original vector-flight game about guiding a small lander down a cliff face to a flat landing pad. Gravity pulls constantly, thrust comes in short bursts, and the pad is small, so the descent must be planned from the top. The game is quiet and tense, with no enemies, only the ground and the pilot's own judgment.

The rules are gentle: turn to face downward, thrust to descend in careful two-step bursts, and fire the lander's beam to clear a single piece of drifting debris. The demo plays a short descent of two thrusts and one clean shot, showing how a controlled fall feels when every burn is deliberate.

Descent pilots burn early and hover late. Short thrusts and a willingness to hang in the air beat a long burn every time, because a lander that arrives too fast cannot slow down in the last step. Restraint, not power, is what lands a spacecraft.

The pantry lanes wind around shelves and crates, and a watchful cat patrols the far side, always walking toward the sound of nibbling. Enemy flyers arrive on a fixed schedule, drifting in from the right, and the patrol must meet each wave on its own row and shoot it down before it passes. Patrol pilots hold their row and let the waves come to them. Move to the next wave's row before it arrives, fire when it is close enough to hit, and never chase a flyer down the pass. The pilots who held the pass longest fired rarely and hit almost every time.

title: Rocket Shield Command
description: Rocket Shield Command is an original gallery game about a shield station defending a small town from falling skyrock. Five targets cross the sky, each worth its own points, and the station has one shot at each. The shield keeper rings a bell for every interception and watches the sky for the next rock.
body:
Rocket Shield Command is an original gallery game about a shield station defending a small town from falling skyrock. Five targets cross the sky, each worth its own points, and the station has one shot at each. The shield keeper rings a bell for every interception and watches the sky for the next rock.

The rules are direct: each round a target sits on a ten-by-ten grid, and you answer with a shot coordinate. A shot on the target or one step away counts as a hit, which forgives a slightly unsteady hand. The demo plays five rounds with four hits and one clean miss.

Shield keepers take the most dangerous rock first and never waste a shot on a distant target when a near one is available. A careful shot at a close target always beats a wild guess at a far one, and the town stays safe when the keeper stays calm.
controls: Type shoot X Y to fire at each target, quit to stop.

demo.code:
import sys
PARAMS = {'targets': [[3, 5, 100], [6, 2, 150], [2, 8, 100], [8, 5, 200], [5, 5, 150]]}
AUTO = ['shoot 3 5', 'shoot 6 2', 'shoot 2 8', 'shoot 8 5', 'shoot 0 0']

def auto_play():
    score, hits = 0, 0
    print("Gallery tribute: auto session")
    for i, target in enumerate(PARAMS["targets"]):
        shot = AUTO[i] if i < len(AUTO) else "shoot 0 0"
        parts = shot.split()
        sx, sy = int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
        tx, ty, pts = target
        hit = abs(sx - tx) <= 1 and abs(sy - ty) <= 1
        if hit:
            score += pts
            hits += 1
        print("Round %d: target %s shot (%d,%d) %s score %d" % (i + 1, (tx, ty), sx, sy, "HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))

def play():
    score, hits = 0, 0
    print("Gallery tribute: type 'shoot X Y' each round, or quit. Targets are on a 0-9 grid.")
    for i, target in enumerate(PARAMS["targets"]):
        print("Round %d: a target has appeared somewhere on the 0-9 grid." % (i + 1))
        got = False
        for line in sys.stdin:
            cmd = line.strip().lower()
            if cmd == "quit":
                print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
                print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))
                return
            parts = cmd.split()
            if len(parts) != 3 or parts[0] != "shoot":
                print("Use: shoot X Y")
                continue
            try:
                sx, sy = int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
            except ValueError:
                print("Use numbers: shoot X Y")
                continue
            tx, ty, pts = target
            hit = abs(sx - tx) <= 1 and abs(sy - ty) <= 1
            if hit:
                score += pts
                hits += 1
            print("%s score %d" % ("HIT" if hit else "MISS", score))
            got = True
            break
        if not got:
            break
    print("FINAL SCORE: %d" % score)
    print("RESULT: HITS %d/%d" % (hits, len(PARAMS["targets"])))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "--play" in sys.argv:
        play()
    else:
        auto_play()

description: Tunnel Digger Dan is an original maze game about a cheerful miner digging tunnels through a hillside in search of gold seams. The hillside lanes wind around boulders and old supports, and a wandering cave bat patrols the far tunnels, always flying toward the sound of digging. Every gold seam adds points, and Dan wins by clearing the hillside without meeting the bat.
body:
Tunnel Digger Dan is an original maze game about a cheerful miner digging tunnels through a hillside in search of gold seams. The hillside lanes wind around boulders and old supports, and a wandering cave bat patrols the far tunnels, always flying toward the sound of digging. Every gold seam adds points, and Dan wins by clearing the hillside without meeting the bat.

The rules are simple: move through the tunnels, step on gold seams for ten points each, and avoid the bat, who costs a life and sends you back to the mine entrance if you meet. You have three lives, and the hillside is cleared when every seam is collected.

Dan digs the near tunnels first and saves the far seam for last, when the bat's patrol is predictable. Never enter a dead-end tunnel while the bat is close, and always leave a second way out. The mine rewards a planned dig far more than a frantic one.

title: Star Swarm
description: Star Swarm is an original fixed shooter about defending a star station from a swirling formation of sky mites. Four columns of mites in three rows drift down toward the station, and your turret slides along the hull to blast them. The swarm is fast, the station is fragile, and the turret's fire is the only thing between them.
body:
Star Swarm is an original fixed shooter about defending a star station from a swirling formation of sky mites. Four columns of mites in three rows drift down toward the station, and your turret slides along the hull to blast them. The swarm is fast, the station is fragile, and the turret's fire is the only thing between them.

The rules are clean: move left or right, fire upward, and clear every mite before it reaches the hull line. A shot destroys the lowest mite in your column, so finishing one column before starting the next is the fastest path to a clear sky. The demo plays a near-complete defense with ten of twelve mites destroyed.

Swarm defense rewards finishing columns. A column with one mite left is a distraction that pulls your eye while the rest of the swarm advances, so clear columns completely and in order. The turrets that held the station were the ones that never left a job half done.
controls: Type left/right/shoot to move and fire, quit to stop.

title: Sky Lance Duel
description: Sky Lance Duel is an original platform game about two knights dueling across a castle walkway, where the walkway itself is the challenge. Two high ledges block the fourteen-step course, and the duelist must jump each one cleanly while keeping momentum for the final stretch. The castle banners flutter, the crowd watches from below, and the duel is decided by footwork.
body:
Sky Lance Duel is an original platform game about two knights dueling across a castle walkway, where the walkway itself is the challenge. Two high ledges block the fourteen-step course, and the duelist must jump each one cleanly while keeping momentum for the final stretch. The castle banners flutter, the crowd watches from below, and the duel is decided by footwork.

The rules are simple: each tick you run or jump, and a jump carries you over two steps, so jumping just before a ledge clears it cleanly. Running into a ledge costs a life, but the duel continues, and reaching the far end wins. The demo plays a clean duel with all three lives intact.

Duelists jump before the ledge, not on it, and keep their momentum through the whole course. A duelist who hesitates at a ledge loses the rhythm, while one who trusts the jump clears it without thinking. Footwork wins the duel long before the lance ever matters.
controls: Type jump/run each tick to clear obstacles, quit to stop.

title: Neon Web
description: Neon Web is an original vector-flight game about a small ship weaving through a glowing web of energy strands in deep space. The strands hang like a net, and the ship's beam can cut through them, but large strands split into smaller ones that drift on. The web glows in the dark, and the ship's path through it is a careful thread.
body:
Neon Web is an original vector-flight game about a small ship weaving through a glowing web of energy strands in deep space. The strands hang like a net, and the ship's beam can cut through them, but large strands split into smaller ones that drift on. The web glows in the dark, and the ship's path through it is a careful thread.

The rules are clean: turn, thrust, and shoot, with large strands splitting into two smaller ones when cut. You have three lives, and touching a strand costs one. The demo plays a flight that cuts one smaller strand and the large strand, while the large strand's pieces drift onward.

Web pilots cut the large strands first and from a distance, because their fragments are the real danger. Break a strand, drift clear of the split, and never sit still in the middle of the web. The ships that wove through were the ones that kept moving.
controls: Type thrust/left/right/shoot to fly and fire, quit to stop.
